summary: Unprefixed lazəm under the inherited Preterit Intransitive label can express present or prospective necessity. The box name does not establish past reference; 17/2 also denotes current need.
17/2 Lazəmli i maǧmuʕa and JTM 5.1/5 ləzamla mede have an l-coded needer and an unmarked nominal requirement. They do not demonstrate two unmarked participants.
Infectum forms with -me/-la are distributed across the inherited senses 1 and 2. Retained filing is provisional; no structural relabeling is justified before suffix analysis.
Existential kət-/lat- plus lazəm, and latat lazəm, can involve nominal/adjectival necessity. These do not establish a new inflected verb sense or a new box.
77/103 lazme yo aʕlayye has adjective-like morphology and an ʕal-marked obligee; withheld as a verbal example pending category analysis. Stem II has no new occurrence evidence.
Personal ləzmatli at 60/173 is kept provisionally in Preterit Intransitive sense 1, following its overt second-person shape. Its temporal value is future-contingent.

The Jan collection contains interviews and direct speech as well as written exposition; it is not uniformly a learned literary register. Modal necessity predominates in the supplied 150 records. No Stem II or Detransitive evidence appears.

lazəm in the inherited Preterit Intransitive box expresses present or prospective obligation, as in Jan 2.1/3 and Jan 4.II/744. Keep the inherited box without deriving past time from its name. Bare finite complements occur beside d-clauses.

The reader overidentifies personal need when a person is merely the topic of a necessity clause: Jan 2.12/3081, 2.35/5570–5571 and 5592 belong with sense 2. aḥna before singular klozəm at 2.16/3587 likewise does not demonstrate personal agreement.

luzamwole/kluzamwole and ləzamwolan combine a needed item with a suffixed needer. kləzmiləxne at Jan 1.36/1506 deserves morphological comparison with kluzamme at 1.15/586 and 1.39/1747; no suffix segmentation is silently normalized.

Jan 1.50/2348 kətwolle lazəm is withheld as a nominal/adjectival necessity expression. raḏayto lə klozəm at 4.II/942 has a feminine nominal requirement with a singular masculine-shaped necessity predicate; it does not identify a personal experiencer.

Confirm the suffixes of kluzamme, luzamxu and kləzmiləxne (Jan 1.15/586, 1.23/1211, 1.36/1506); which are agreement, l-coded needers, and resumptive needed items?
Does u ḥa d luzamwo at Jan 1.28/1322 establish personal Infectum-wa, or an elliptical impersonal necessity construction? What precisely was needed?
Confirm the category of lazəm inside kətwolle lazəm (Jan 1.50/2348); should nominal/adjectival necessity have its own descriptive treatment?
Needers include houses, a translation task and a melon plot, as well as persons. The nominal requirement can be materials, time or a quantity of ploughings; no independent new meaning follows.
Jan repeatedly supports the round 1 modal gloss clarification: obligation with d-clauses or bare finite predicates, including negative and plural clauses. No additional numbered sense is needed.

gədləzmo lu medano has a feminine personal predicate referring to the sister in a coordinated alternative and an l-marked requirement. This supports round 1’s distinction from suffixed impersonal need.
